question.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+6y=10 \\ 3x+9y=21.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
question.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 10 \\ 3 & 9 & 21\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 10 \\ 3 & 9 & 21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 5 \\ 3 & 9 & 21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+3y=5 \\ 0x+0y=6.\end{aligned}
$$

However, the final equation $0x+0y=6$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=6,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.
